Contendathon

Try trades before you make them. Pick a team and the players it gets from anyone in the league, then Evaluate move. The rest of the season is replayed with the very same simulated player weeks, so every change on the page comes from the moves: each number shows its change in parentheses, green when it's better for that team. Moves stack in order, each from its starting week; × removes one. A trade is two moves (one each way). The betting lines are hidden while the analyzer is on. Lineups are re-picked by projection every week; rosters over the limit aren't trimmed. Data as of this page's last update.

      This week's linesLines straight from the simulation: every game played out times. The moneyline is the fair price for each side's win chance (no bookmaker cut), e.g. −150 means risk 150 to win 100, +150 means risk 100 to win 150. The spread is the median simulated margin and the over/under the median combined score, both rounded to the half point. Avg = the team's simulated average score.

Points ScoredActual points scored so far, then each team's average score across all simulations: the best lineup by Sleeper's projections, with every starter's score drawn around his Sleeper projection, using how far real 2024–26 scores swung around projections.Each team's chance to win the championship going into every week played so far, then today. A week's point is the league as it stood before that week's games, with each player as of his own kickoff: results through the week before, the lineups teams had when their players locked, and every projection as it stood just before that player's game. The last point is today's odds, as shown on the rest of the page. The trade analyzer doesn't change it.

      Playoff pictureThe rest of the season played out many thousands of times, player by player: each starter's score is drawn from how players at his position and projection level really scored against their projections in 2024–26, rescaled so his average is exactly his Sleeper projection.       Projected final pointsMost projected points first. All-play is the record a team would have if it played every other team every week; luck is actual wins minus all-play expected wins, so a positive number means the schedule has been kind.

      SchedulePlayed weeks (left of the line): the chance the model gave each team before kickoff, from Sleeper's projections that week for the lineup it actually started. Green when the favorite won (the projection was right), red when the underdog won. Remaining weeks: the share of simulations in which the team outscores that opponent; cyan leans toward a win, red toward a loss. Average win chance and projected wins count remaining games only.

      Rosters by weekEvery skill player on a roster and what he scored or is projected to score. Played weeks show the lineup the team actually started; the ✓ column marks the max PF lineup, so an orange ✓ on the bench is points left there. Future weeks show the best lineup by projections on today's roster, with the range each player lands in 80% of the time around his projection.

      Tankathon tab: rows in max PF slot order. The total row's 80% range is the week's max PF before kickoff: the whole roster simulated from that week's projections, the best lineup picked in each simulation. For the week in progress, the rows are the max PF lineup with projections filled in for players who haven't played yet (the larger of points so far and projection mid-game). In the header, max PF so far is the best lineup from points already scored (a player whose game hasn't started counts 0), so it can only go up; projected is the simulated average: games already played as scored, the rest simulated.

      Projected top scorersEvery projected NFL QB, RB, WR and TE, rostered or not. The rest of the regular season is the sum of Sleeper's weekly projections, which is exactly what the simulation averages to. Season = points so far plus that. Weekly range = where his week lands 80% of the time, from real weeks of players projected near him; hover it for the details. Click a column to sort; click a rostered player to highlight his team.

      Max PF (the best lineup the roster could have started, picked after the games) minus points actually scored. Lower is better; the percentage is how much of max PF the team actually started. Like the league's max PF, this counts taxi and IR players, who can't actually be started.

      For each week played, the best lineup by projections was built from the roster the team had that week and compared to the points it actually scored.       Notes on these numbers
      • Only regular-season weeks (through week ) count.
      • Projected weeks assume each manager starts the best lineup by projections from today's roster (IR included), and that nobody new gets hurt. Trades, waivers and injuries will move every line.
      • In the roster table, "Projected" is Sleeper's raw number. "Taxi slot" and "IR slot" show where each player sits on his fantasy roster today; the filled tags (IR, PUP, Out, D, Q...) are his NFL injury designation, whatever slot he's in: Sleeper's today for games still to play; for a finished game, shown only if he didn't play (his status at kickoff, else Out). "est." marks a player whose game hadn't finished, so his projection stands in for his score.
      • Sources: Sleeper league data and Sleeper's weekly player projections, scored with this league's settings; NFL game status from ESPN.
